newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica coffee crop ends at 2.7 mln 60-kg bags.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica coffee crop ends at 2.7 mln 60-kg bags.

text.p: Costa Rica ended its 1996-1997 coffee campaign with a crop of 2.7 million 60-kg bags, similar to last cycle, the executive director of the Costa Rican Coffee Institute said.

Guillermo Canet told Reuters that exports to April 7 had totaled 1,533,000 bags. He said available exportable production from this cycle was around 700,000 bags and the remainder would go for internal consumption.

It appears that fears that the Costa Rican harvest would drop to 2.3 million bags never materialised. The institute predicted in January that output would fall because of a cyclical dip and damage from Hurricane Ceasr last autumn.

Canet said for the 1997-1998 crop the preliminary calculation was that another 2.7 million bags was expected to be produced. Canet said the country had already sold 245,000 bags for September and October deliveries from that crop.
Costa Rica's crop peters out in March after peaking around November and December. In low-lying regions it starts in June, whereas high elevations are harvested much later.
